domain_setting: A calm editorial roadside world covering a personal automobile, its visible components, routine maintenance, workshop visits, driving maneuvers, street parking, traffic, and practical vehicle documents.
recurring_scale_anchors: Use a 304x192 stage with the main object contained within x=24..280 and y=18..174.
Road and workshop floors sit near y=148; car wheels are bold enough to read at small card size.
For part-of-car cards, ghost the rest of the automobile in pale slate and illuminate only the target part.
Drivers and mechanics are shown as adult figures with compact, volumetric limbs; no stick figures.
Documents, dashboard gauges, street signs, meters, and clocks contain no readable words, letters, numerals, brands, or license plates.
Use a generic car orientation; avoid location-specific road rules.

polysemy_resolution_table.battery: The rechargeable electrical battery under a car hood, not a military artillery unit or group of musicians.
polysemy_resolution_table.car: A passenger road automobile; the glossary alternate for streetcar is resolved by the Driving a car chapter.
polysemy_resolution_table.engine: A car power unit with visible mechanical components, not a person who runs an organization or a locomotive.
polysemy_resolution_table.headlight: The forward lamp on a car, shown lighting the road ahead; not a railway headlamp.
polysemy_resolution_table.hood (car): The hinged panel covering the front engine compartment (bonnet), not clothing worn over a head.
polysemy_resolution_table.turn signal / indicator (uk, for a turn: The amber lamp on the car corner that flashes to show a turn; indicator is UK wording.
polysemy_resolution_table.oil (car): Motor oil used to lubricate an automobile engine, not cooking oil or crude oil.
polysemy_resolution_table.tire: The rubber wheel covering on a car, despite the glossary verb meaning exhaust someone.
polysemy_resolution_table.trunk (car): The enclosed rear luggage compartment of a car, not a tree trunk.
polysemy_resolution_table.diesel: Diesel fuel at a vehicle pump, distinguished from gasoline by pump hardware, not typography.
polysemy_resolution_table.fill up: Fill a car's fuel tank at a pump, not fill a container in general.
polysemy_resolution_table.fuel: Automotive fuel supplied to a car, represented at a pump, not motivation or food.
polysemy_resolution_table.garage: A private enclosed building for storing a car, distinct from the commercial repair shop.
polysemy_resolution_table.gasoline / gas: Petrol for an automobile, distinct from gaseous fuel and the gas station itself.
polysemy_resolution_table.gas station: A roadside business where cars refuel, distinct from the fuel or its pump.
polysemy_resolution_table.driving: Operating a motor vehicle on the road, not mechanically powering a device.
polysemy_resolution_table.drop someone off: Drive a passenger to a destination and let them out at the curb.
polysemy_resolution_table.indicate: Use the vehicle turn indicator before changing direction; separate from the broader visible signal cue.
polysemy_resolution_table.pass (overtake) / overtake: Drive past a slower car in the same direction on a clear road, not pass an object by walking.
polysemy_resolution_table.park (vehicle): Leave a vehicle stationary in a legal parking space, not a public park.
polysemy_resolution_table.pick someone up: Stop the car at the curb and let a waiting passenger get in, the inverse of drop someone off.
polysemy_resolution_table.set off: Begin a car journey by pulling away from a driveway or curb.
polysemy_resolution_table.signal: Give a road user a turn or lane-change signal with the car's indicator, distinct from the broader verb indicate scene.
polysemy_resolution_table.parking attendant: A person who guides cars or checks parking in a lot, not a parking meter.
polysemy_resolution_table.parking lot: An outdoor or multi-bay area where cars are left, not a roadside meter or private garage.
polysemy_resolution_table.parking meter: A curbside device used to pay for a timed parking space; display has icon-only marks.
polysemy_resolution_table.parking ticket: A penalty notice tucked under a car wiper after an illegal parking violation, not an admission or travel ticket.
polysemy_resolution_table.pedestrian crossing: A marked road crossing where people walk across, with cars stopped behind the line.
polysemy_resolution_table.road sign: A roadside information or warning panel, shown with a simple shape/symbol and no letters.
polysemy_resolution_table.speed camera: A roadside camera that records a speeding car, not a traffic-light camera.
polysemy_resolution_table.speed limit: The maximum permitted road speed, communicated with a generic circular sign and visual marker but no numerals.
polysemy_resolution_table.traffic jam: A slow or stopped queue of cars caused by congestion, not a parking lot.
polysemy_resolution_table.traffic lights: A road signal with red, amber, and green lamps controlling intersecting traffic.
polysemy_resolution_table.break down: A car suffers a mechanical failure and stops at the roadside, not emotionally collapse or dismantle an object.
polysemy_resolution_table.car accident: The crash scene involving two vehicles with a small, non-graphic impact cue; no injury or damage detail.
polysemy_resolution_table.driver's license: A government driving permit card with a portrait and abstract security marks, containing no legible identity data.
polysemy_resolution_table.flat tire: A deflated car tire visibly squashed against the road, distinct from a general breakdown.
polysemy_resolution_table.have a car accident: A driver experiences a minor collision; show the person and car together to teach the event phrase.
polysemy_resolution_table.insurance: A car insurance policy represented by a protected vehicle and shield/document, not health or life insurance.
polysemy_resolution_table.registration: Vehicle registration papers or a vehicle document attached to the car, not a person registering for an event.

sibling_contrasts.car parts: Car is the whole vehicle. Battery, brakes, engine, headlight, hood, turn signal, oil, seatbelt, steering wheel, tire, trunk, and windshield each isolate one functional part with the body ghosted or in supporting context.
sibling_contrasts.maintenance: Auto repair shop and repair shop both show a commercial car workshop, but auto repair shop gets a clearer lift and vehicle cue. Car wash cleans the body; oil change replaces engine oil; check oil and check tires are inspection actions; service the car combines routine inspection and maintenance.
sibling_contrasts.fuel: Fuel is the broad automotive supply; gasoline and diesel are distinct fuels; gas station is the place; fill up is the action of pumping fuel into a tank.
sibling_contrasts.driving_actions: Drop someone off ends a ride at the curb; pick someone up begins one. Set off begins a journey; park ends movement. Slow down and speed up use contrasting motion cues. Pass/overtake shows one car moving ahead of another.
sibling_contrasts.traffic_and_parking: Parking lot is a place, meter is the payment device, attendant is the person, and parking ticket is the consequence. Traffic lights control an intersection; speed camera detects speed; road sign provides guidance; speed limit states a cap; traffic jam shows congestion.
sibling_contrasts.accident_documents: Car accident is the collision scene; have a car accident includes the driver and event. Break down is mechanical failure without collision; flat tire is one concrete failure. License permits the driver, registration identifies the vehicle, and insurance protects against costs.

art_direction: Use the course warm-paper, navy-outline editorial style with muted blue-gray vehicle bodywork, sage workshop accents, amber indicator and caution cues, and uncluttered road or garage settings. Make silhouettes and interactions distinct at thumbnail size. Keep road events calm and non-graphic. No readable text, letters, numerals, logos, license plates, or real identity data.
